changelog:
Major update: Overhaul from a localized sales/competitive research tool to a universal customer research skill for product teams and marketers.

- Completely rewritten to focus on two core modes: analyzing existing research assets and gathering new research from digital sources (forums, reviews, communities, etc.)
- Now aligned with modern customer development practices, supporting jobs-to-be-done (JTBD), persona building, and qualitative synthesis.
- Flexible triggers now include VOC, NPS, support analysis, digital watering hole mining, review mining, and more.
- Explicitly covers B2B, B2C, SMB, developer, and enterprise research use cases; includes ICP-specific source recommendations.
- Embedded quality guardrails: Confidence levels, bias checks, and recency windows required for all insights.
- File structure simplified: legacy scripts and specialized report generators removed; new reference guides added.
summary: When the user wants to conduct, analyze, or synthesize customer research. Use when the user mentions "customer research," "ICP research," "talk to customers," "analyze transcripts," "customer interviews," "survey analysis," "support ticket analysis," "voice of customer," "VOC," "build personas," "customer personas," "jobs to be done," "JTBD," "what do customers say," "what are customers struggling with," "Reddit mining," "G2 reviews," "review mining," "digital watering holes," "community research," "forum research," "competitor reviews," "customer sentiment," or "find out why customers churn/convert/buy." Use for both analyzing existing research assets AND gathering new research from online sources. For writing copy informed by research, see copywriting. For acting on research to improve pages, see cro.
